taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes it was previously treated as a synonym or subspecies of the hoary marmot (M. caligata).
fieldMarks: Black fur on top of the head from nose to neck; coarse brown and black back
21-26 in. long, 5.5-8.8 lb; males slightly larger than females
Bushy tail; short muscular legs, small round eyes, broad rounded ears
behavior: Colonies of up to 50, each with its own den
Hibernates about late August to early June, waking every 3-4 weeks
Sentinel alarm calls vary by predator
Eats grasses, forbs, legumes and fruit near burrows
habitat: Boulder fields and talus slopes with large rocks next to productive tundra, about 3,250-4,000 ft.
range: Brooks Range of northern Alaska, perhaps also northern Yukon (unconfirmed).
